name: Deepgram Voice Agent API
positioning: Deepgram is a speech AI vendor whose Voice Agent API orchestrates speech recognition, an LLM and text-to-speech over one WebSocket for developers building voice agents.

pricing.model: Per-minute of WebSocket connection time, tiered by which LLM and TTS are used and whether you bring your own; pay-as-you-go or prepaid Growth plan.
pricing.headline: Standard tier $0.075/min pay-as-you-go ($0.068/min Growth); bring-your-own LLM and TTS from $0.050/min ($0.041/min Growth); Advanced tier $0.163/min.
planNotes: Tiers (pay-as-you-go / Growth per minute): Standard 0.075 / 0.068; Standard with BYO TTS 0.065 / 0.051; Custom BYO LLM 0.065 / 0.059; Custom BYO LLM and TTS 0.050 / 0.041; Advanced 0.163 / 0.146; Advanced BYO TTS 0.122 / 0.110.
Billing is by conversation (WebSocket connection) duration and covers STT, LLM and TTS orchestration; with a bring-your-own LLM you pay Deepgram for the audio components and orchestration.
Growth plan starts at $4K+ per year of prepaid credits with savings of up to 20%.
Voice agent concurrency is up to 45 (pay-as-you-go) or 60 (Growth) via WebSocket.

Verified on the HTML pricing page and the machine-readable markdown version of the same page; the HTML rendering was ambiguous for the Custom BYO LLM row, so the markdown values were used. Both are Deepgram's own pages.
pricing.freeTrial: $200 free credit for new accounts, no credit card required.
whatIsExtra: Telephony and phone numbers are not part of the Voice Agent API; they come from a telephony provider
Third-party LLM or TTS usage if you bring your own

strengths.claim: Own speech recognition models (Flux and Nova-3) with built-in turn detection designed for voice agents.
Transparent tiered per-minute pricing with discounts for bringing your own LLM or TTS, and a $200 free credit.
States SOC 2 Type 1 and Type 2, HIPAA business associate status with a BAA on request, GDPR readiness with an EU endpoint, and an Australian endpoint.
Works with telephony providers such as Twilio, plus LiveKit and Pipecat integrations, via documented guides.
Supports function calling, multi-agent handoff and reusable agent configurations.

limitations.claim: Telephony is not included: the docs show bridging calls from a provider such as Twilio to the WebSocket API, so a telephony account and server code are needed.
Billing is by WebSocket connection time and the Voice Agent API is concurrency-limited to 45 on pay-as-you-go.
Compliance documentation such as SOC 2 certificates and a BAA is obtained by contacting Deepgram.

integrations: Third-party LLM providers (bring your own LLM)

compliance.note: Stated by vendor, self-attested: docs state SOC 2 Type 1 and 2, GDPR readiness with EU endpoint, HIPAA business-associate status with a BAA on request, plus CCPA and PCI. Certificates and the BAA are available on request, not public.

telephony.providedNumbers: None found: Deepgram provides the speech and agent layer, and the docs connect it to your own telephony provider (for example a Twilio number).

stepsToLeave: Agent behaviour is defined by the Settings message (STT, LLM, TTS, prompt, functions) that your own code sends, so the configuration already lives in your codebase.
Reusable agent configurations stored with Deepgram are documented as being created and reused through the API.
Telephony stays with your own provider; repoint the number's media stream to the new platform there.

bestFor: Engineering teams building their own voice-agent stack who want Deepgram's speech models and a single orchestration socket, and who will supply telephony and application logic themselves.
